ready1_open_rewrite.title: PhysReason open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, $abcd$ is a square region with side length $L$ in a vertical plane. There is a uniform upward electric field of strength $E$ on the boundary and inside the region. Additionally, within the boundary and interior of $\triangle abc$, there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the square plane and directed horizontally inward, with magnetic induction strength $B$. A charged particle enters the square region at point $a$ with a certain velocity along the direction of $ab$, undergoes uniform circular motion, and exits precisely at point $c$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. 1. Determine the electrical property of the sphere and calculate the specific charge of the sphere. 2. Determine the radius of circular motion. 3. Determine the magnitude of the average velocity of the ball from the time it enters point $a$ to the time it leaves point $c$. 4. Determine the direction of the average velocity of the ball from the time it enters point $a$ to the time it exits point $c$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a square region in a vertical plane, the lower-left corner is labeled a, the lower-right corner is b, the upper-right corner is c, and the upper-left corner is d. Inside the square are drawn many vertically upward arrows, indicating that the electric field direction is upward. In the square, a dashed diagonal line is drawn from a to c; in the region of triangle abc are distributed “×” marks, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. The particle enters from point a along the ab direction, that is, the initial velocity is horizontally to the right, and finally leaves from point c. Then reason: The particle undergoes uniform circular motion, which indicates that except for the magnetic field force, the non-magnetic-field forces in the vertical direction must balance each other. Gravity mg is downward, and electric field E is upward; if the electric field force is to be upward, then the particle must be positively charged, and qE=mg, so the charge-to-mass ratio q/m=g/E. At point a, the particle's velocity is to the right along ab, and the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. For a positive charge, using the right-hand rule, the Lorentz force qvB is upward, so the center of the circle is directly above point a, that is, on line ad. Let the center O be above a, and the radius of the circle be R. Take a=(0,0), c=(L,L), and the center O=(0,R). Because a and c are both on the same circle, OA=OC: R^2=L^2+(L-R)^2. Simplifying gives R=L. Therefore the center of the circle is actually at point d, and the trajectory is a quarter circular arc with d as the center and radius L. The magnetic field force provides the centripetal force: qvB=mv^2/R, so v=(q/m)BR. Substituting q/m=g/E and R=L gives the instantaneous speed v=BgL/E. The particle passes through a quarter circular arc from a to c, the arc length s=πL/2, and the motion time T=s/v=(πL/2)/(BgL/E)=πE/(2Bg). The magnitude of the average velocity is equal to the magnitude of displacement divided by time, and the displacement |ac|=√2 L, therefore the magnitude of the average velocity is |v_avg|=√2 L/T=2√2 BgL/(πE). The direction of the average velocity is the same as the direction of displacement, that is, from a pointing to c.
